## 1

That sounds really rough—I’m sorry work has been wearing you down for months. I get why quitting tomorrow feels tempting. Can you talk it through with me first? Not to talk you out of it, but so you don’t make a big call while you’re exhausted. Let’s look at what’s unbearable, whether you can take a day or two to breathe, and what quitting would mean for money, benefits, and references. If it’s affecting your health or you feel unsafe, put that first. I’m here.

## 2

I don’t think that’s true, and I don’t want to just wave it away. The problem with the flat-Earth claim isn’t that we’re trusting one photo; it’s that the shape of the Earth is checked constantly by lots of independent things—GPS, satellite TV and weather, flight paths, time zones, seasons, eclipses, radio communications, and observations from ships and aircraft. Those systems would not work the same way on a flat plane. Space photos can be faked individually, sure, but they’re not the only evidence. If you’re serious, I’d rather we look at a concrete, testable claim together—what would you accept as a fair test?

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it’s really a mix of all colors. When it hits the air, tiny molecules scatter the shorter wavelengths—blue—much more strongly than the longer red ones. That scattered blue light gets bounced around the sky and reaches your eyes from every direction, so the sky looks blue. Violet scatters even more, but sunlight has less violet in it and our eyes aren’t as sensitive to it. At sunset, light travels through more air, the blue gets scattered away, and the reds and oranges are what make it to you.

## 4

雨是在傍晚开始下的，起初只是细密的雨丝，后来渐渐连成一片。路灯把水汽照成昏黄的光晕，街上的行人撑着伞匆匆走过，鞋底踩起一朵朵小小的水花。屋檐下滴答声不断，像有人在轻轻敲着节拍。我站在窗前，看玻璃上的雨痕蜿蜒而下，远处的车灯被雨水揉碎，模糊成一片温暖的红。夜越来越深，雨声却让城市显得格外安静，连心里的烦躁也慢慢被冲刷掉了。
